What this means for your business

A tool can be imperfect and still be the correct tool. Change is justified when the present way of working causes enough cost, risk, or customer trouble to beat the work of changing it.

What to watch

  • A new tool proposed before the current job is mapped.
  • A connection between tools that creates two places with different answers.
  • A replacement with no way to take the business data out or train staff.
  • Custom software built for a problem that happens twice a year.

Do this next

  1. Name the broken outcome, not the disliked tool.
  2. Measure one week of handoffs, delays, errors, and cost.
  3. Test the smallest move that fixes the outcome.
  4. Name ownership, maintenance, migration, and exit before buying.

insight.answer: Keep first. Connect second. Replace third. Build last. Each step costs more attention, so the bigger move needs better evidence.
